questions.question: Describe the maximum and minimum of a day's temperature graph, giving position and meaning.
questions.expected_answer: The maximum is in the mid-afternoon, when the temperature is highest; the minimum is just before dawn, when it is lowest. The graph increases from dawn to the maximum and decreases from there to the minimum.

questions.question: Why is the cost-against-tickets graph drawn as dots while the depth-against-time graph of a bath is a line?
questions.expected_answer: Tickets are counted: there is no cost for two and a half tickets, so the points are not joined. Depth and time are measurements that take every value in between, so the graph is an unbroken line.

questions.question: What is the difference between a local maximum and the global maximum?
questions.expected_answer: A local maximum is the top of any hill on the graph; the global maximum is the highest point of the whole graph, which may be the tallest hill or an end point.
